reviews.scope: Interpret tangent values, special angles, and excluded undefined inputs.
reviews.reason: Defining principal inverse tangent on (-pi/2, pi/2) and solving tan(x)=t directly requires knowing the tangent function, its special values, and the excluded angles where cosine is zero.

reviews.scope: Evaluate sums of inverse-tangent angles via the tangent addition formula.
reviews.reason: Computing a sum of inverse-tangent angles by taking the tangent of the sum relies on the tangent addition formula, whereas single-angle tangent equations do not.
reviews.counterexample: Direct solving of tan(x)=t in an interval requires only principal arctangent and periodicity without angle-sum formulas.

reviews.scope: Understand domain restriction for a one-to-one inverse and avoid reciprocal confusion.
reviews.reason: General bijection criteria and distinguishing functional inverses from reciprocals prepare students to restrict tangent to (-pi/2, pi/2), though arctangent can be used directly from its unique-angle definition.
reviews.counterexample: One can apply the explicit definition of Arctan(t) as the unique angle in (-pi/2, pi/2) with tangent t without solving affine inverses.

reviews.scope: Define line-to-line distance as the minimum distance between point pairs.
reviews.reason: Defining the distance between two lines as the minimum of |P-Q| over points on each line directly requires the definition of distance between two points.

reviews.scope: Distinguish intersecting, parallel, and skew spatial lines when analyzing minimum distance.
reviews.reason: The mastery criteria explicitly require checking coplanarity and distinguishing skew lines from intersecting or parallel lines so nonparallel spatial lines are not assumed to have zero distance.

reviews.scope: Connect the general line-distance definition with the planar parallel-line distance formula.
reviews.reason: The coordinate formula for parallel planar lines computes separation in one special case, while the general set-to-set minimum distance definition holds geometrically without coordinate line equations.
reviews.counterexample: Minimum distance between lines can be defined and evaluated geometrically in plane or space without using general-form linear equations.

reviews.scope: Understand why two distinct points, unlike one point, fix a line.
reviews.reason: Knowing that two distinct points determine a unique line motivates why two points in a plane fix the whole line, though plane containment itself is a separate incidence axiom.
reviews.counterexample: The incidence axiom can be applied directly to a given line with two distinct points in a plane without invoking segment length or line-uniqueness proofs.

reviews.scope: Connect the two-point line-containment axiom with the other plane incidence axioms.
reviews.reason: Three-point plane determination and two-plane intersection are sibling incidence axioms in solid geometry; neither is logically required to state or apply two-point line-plane containment.
reviews.counterexample: Applying two-point line containment in a given plane does not require constructing a plane from three points or intersecting two planes.

reviews.scope: Connect two-point containment with the three-way classification of line-plane positions.
reviews.reason: Classifying line-plane positions into containment, single-point intersection, and parallelism links directly to the containment axiom, though the axiom usually precedes full line-plane and plane-plane classification.
reviews.counterexample: One can deduce that every point of a line lies in a plane from two shared points without first studying plane-plane relative positions.

reviews.scope: Plot test points and represent solution sets in the Cartesian coordinate plane.
reviews.reason: Graphing planar linear inequalities as half-planes and checking test-point coordinates inherently requires understanding the Cartesian coordinate system and point coordinates.

reviews.scope: Interpret general two-variable linear equations as boundary lines of half-planes.
reviews.reason: Knowing that Ax+By+C=0 represents any planar line prepares students to graph inequality boundaries, though boundaries can also be graphed from slope-intercept or coordinate-intercept forms without point-slope conversion.
reviews.counterexample: Boundary lines can be plotted directly from intercept pairs or slope-intercept form without converting from point-slope form.

reviews.scope: Find candidate polygon vertices by solving pairs of boundary line equations.
reviews.reason: Locating feasible polygon vertices and testing redundant cuts algebraically relies on solving pairwise boundary line equations, whereas graphical shading or variable elimination can identify regions without pairwise equation solving.
reviews.counterexample: Graphical half-plane shading on a grid or inequality elimination can identify feasible regions without algebraically solving simultaneous boundary equations.

reviews.scope: Use the definitions of a circle, its center, and its constant radius.
reviews.reason: Finding the nearest point on a circle and deriving the radial distance |OX-r| directly requires the definition of a circle as points at constant radius r from center O.

reviews.scope: Prove the minimum radial distance bound |OX-r| using triangle side inequalities.
reviews.reason: The geometric proof that any non-radial circle point P satisfies XP > |OX-r| uses the triangle side-difference inequality on triangle OXP, whereas analytic or cosine-law derivations avoid it.
reviews.counterexample: Minimizing XP^2 = OX^2 + r^2 - 2*OX*r*cos(theta) over angle theta establishes the radial minimum without invoking triangle side inequalities.

reviews.scope: Understand whole-number multiplication notation and the meaning of multiplying factors.
reviews.reason: Evaluating products of nonnegative integers inherently requires understanding the multiplication operation, its notation, and its foundational meaning on whole numbers.

reviews.scope: Apply single-digit multiplication facts from 2 to 6 during product evaluation.
reviews.reason: Evaluating products through single-digit table lookups uses the 2-to-6 multiplication facts whenever those factors are paired, whereas repeated addition or alternative factor groupings can bypass specific table pairs.
reviews.counterexample: A product can be evaluated by repeated addition or by pairing factors into tens instead of invoking a specific 2-to-6 table fact.

reviews.scope: Apply single-digit multiplication facts for 7, 8, and 9 during evaluation.
reviews.reason: Direct table-fact evaluation uses the 7, 8, and 9 multiplication facts when those factors are paired, while regrouping factors into tens or repeated addition avoids them.
reviews.counterexample: In 5*8*2, regrouping as (5*2)*8 = 10*8 = 80 avoids using the 5*8 table fact.

reviews.scope: Multiply an intermediate multi-digit partial product by a one-digit factor.
reviews.reason: Successive multiplication that produces a multi-digit intermediate product uses the multi-digit by one-digit place-value algorithm, whereas factor regrouping or mental decomposition can avoid written column multiplication.
reviews.counterexample: Mental doubling or regrouping factors into tens avoids the written multi-digit by one-digit column algorithm.

reviews.scope: Reorder and regroup factors using commutative and associative multiplication laws.
reviews.reason: Reordering or reassociating factors to simplify a multi-factor product relies on the commutative and associative properties of multiplication, while multiplying sequentially in the written order does not.
reviews.counterexample: Evaluating a product strictly from left to right in the given order requires no commutative or associative regrouping.

reviews.scope: Multiply a tens factor formed by pairing 5 and 2 using trailing-zero rules.
reviews.reason: Pairing 5 and 2 produces a factor ending in zero whose product uses the trailing-zero multiplication rule, whereas routes without zero-digit factors or using general multiplication avoid it.
reviews.counterexample: Products without zero-ending intermediate factors, such as 4*4*6, or general column multiplication do not use the trailing-zero shortcut.

reviews.scope: Determine where folded paper cells land across a crease using reflection symmetry.
reviews.reason: Tracking layers during paper folding uses reflection symmetry across the crease to pair source and destination cell positions, whereas abstract stack push-pop simulations do not involve geometric reflection.
reviews.counterexample: Simulating last-in-first-out stack push and pop sequences requires only order tracking without reflection symmetry.
